key_insight: D-OPSD introduces on-policy self-distillation to continuously fine-tune step-distilled (few-step) diffusion models without degrading their fast, few-step inference quality — the model learns from its own on-policy trajectories to preserve and improve step-wise behavior.
problem_solved: Standard supervised fine-tuning breaks the inference behavior of step-distilled few-step diffusion models due to train/inference mismatch; D-OPSD solves continuous tuning while retaining few-step efficiency and sample quality.
method: On-policy self-distillation loop: generate intermediate trajectories with the current (teacher) few-step model and use them as targets for the student to learn step-wise denoising behavior.
Training objective blends distillation losses that align student predictions with teacher on-policy outputs and supervised task losses, preserving the distilled step schedule.
Continuous/iterative update scheme that updates teacher from the tuned student (or uses moving-average teacher) to maintain consistency and avoid catastrophic changes to few-step inference.
impact: Enables practitioners to safely fine-tune high-speed few-step diffusion models for downstream tasks or data domains while keeping fast inference and high sample quality, reducing the need for costly multi-step retraining.

paper_title: D-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continuously Tuning Step-Distilled Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Dengyang Jiang, Xin Jin, Dongyang Liu, Zanyi Wang, Mingzhe Zheng
